document_type: Survey + formalism + benchmark proposal + small reference experiment. The authors state this explicitly: 'This is a survey: it proposes a formalism and a benchmark protocol but does not provide large-scale empirical validation of either.' [Limitations, first sentence]

problem_stated.as_the_paper_states_it: Four separate research communities — KV-cache compression, prompt/context compression, bounded-state architectures, and agent memory consolidation — each independently solve 'a rate–distortion decision about what context-derived information to retain versus discard, at what fidelity, under a resource budget, so as to preserve downstream task utility.' [Abstract, sentence 4]
problem_stated.the_operational_framing: 'A method at any level takes the history H of everything the model has read and produces a smaller representation Z that fits a budget B; call this the compaction operator C. The model then runs on Z in place of the original, through a usage operator U. Stated or not, the method is solving one optimization: keep Z small while giving up as little downstream accuracy as possible.' [§1, ¶4]
problem_stated.the_three_differences_that_remain: 'What unit do they compress: a bit, a token, an attention head, a span of text, a vector, a stored fact? Where in the model's life do they act: pretraining, prefill, decoding, serving, inside a task, or between tasks? And do they decide what to keep before the query is known, or after?' [§1, ¶4]
problem_stated.scope_restriction: 'We restrict attention to the compaction of memory that comes from a model's context, drawing mostly on work from 2023 to 2026... Weight-level compression (pruning, distillation, weight quantization) is out of scope, as is long-context training that imposes no memory bound, except where such work builds in a bounded memory.' [§1, final ¶]
problem_stated.why_this_matters_for_v2: [해설] This is the only paper in the v2 corpus that states a budget/quality tradeoff as a constrained optimization with a lower bound that is indifferent to which of Θ / W / E holds the state. It is therefore the capacity chapter's formal machinery: the object it bounds is exactly S0 §2.4's C (state capacity).

inherited_open_question.from: Prior agent-memory surveys — [47] 'Memory in the Age of AI Agents' and [66] 'A Survey on Long-Term Memory Security in LLM Agents' — plus the benchmark precursors SCBench [61] and KVPress [84].
inherited_open_question.question: Prior surveys named lossy consolidation and memory integrity as THE open problems of agent memory but did not measure what repeated consolidation costs; and no existing benchmark holds one budget axis across the compaction layers. This paper takes up both: it turns 'lossy consolidation is the open problem' into a falsifiable prediction (super-linear error growth under repeated irreversible summarization) and runs it.
evidence: §7, final subsection 'Reversibility and the compounding of loss': 'Benchmarks such as LOCOMO and LongMemEval probe single-shot recall, multi-session reasoning, and knowledge updates, but not the compounding curve over many consolidation cycles [74, 118]. That gap is why we test it directly in Section 14, and why recent surveys of agent memory and its security flag lossy consolidation and memory integrity as the open problems [47, 66].'

§13.1, final ¶ of 'What exists': 'Two efforts come closest to compaction itself. SCBench studies long-context methods through a KV-cache-centric lens... KVPress [84] supplies a harness that standardizes KV compression... We treat both as direct precursors and build on them rather than around them.'

§13.2: 'Our response is COMPACT-Bench, an extension of SCBench [61] and KVPress rather than a replacement: it keeps their task corpora and KV harness and supplies the axes and task families they leave out.'

§1, ¶6 (positioning against prior surveys): 'We are not the first to connect these areas. One recent survey gathers token-level, parametric, latent, and agent memory under a Forms/Functions/Dynamics scheme [47], and another casts agent memory as a write–manage–read POMDP [31]. What this survey adds is a single optimization objective with a provable bound rather than a descriptive grouping...'
inherited_open_question.what_it_does_NOT_inherit: [평가] It inherits nothing from the Θ-path or the W-path sleep lines. It does not pick up any stated open question from Letta's Sleep-time Compute [65] even though it cites that paper four times, and it never engages the sleep/consolidation literature that names Θ as the write target. See cross_path_citations.

core_mechanism.one_line: A single constrained optimization — pick a compaction operator cmp_Θ that maps the history 𝓗 to a compact state Z of size ≤ C so as to minimize the expected task loss 𝓛 of the downstream reader use(Z, q) — together with a Fano/data-processing lower bound on the error rate that holds for ANY Z, whatever layer (Θ, W, E, or the KV cache) physically holds it.

three_first_class_properties.source: [rate-distortion-compaction §2, ¶6 — 'Three first-class properties separate methods that fail from those that do not.']
three_first_class_properties.P-rev: Reversibility: 'can content dropped by C be re-derived if a later query needs it? Retrieval-backed and archival schemes can; eviction and summarization cannot.'
three_first_class_properties.P-q: Query-conditioning: 'does C see the query (or its distribution) when it decides what to keep? Offline gisting does not; LongLLMLingua and Quest do.'
three_first_class_properties.P-fid: Fidelity profile: 'is the representation lossless, near-lossless, uniformly lossy, or multi-fidelity (a small high-fidelity tier plus a large lossy tier)?'
three_first_class_properties.why_promoted: 'Two schemes can sit at the same budget B and the same average distortion yet behave completely differently on the queries that matter... three properties that Eq. (1) leaves implicit and that we promote to the center of the survey.'

four_falsifiable_predictions.source: [rate-distortion-compaction §2, final ¶ — 'The formalism yields four falsifiable predictions']
four_falsifiable_predictions.1_KV: 'for attention-score eviction, needle recall collapses once the per-token budget falls below the needle's share of attention mass, and the collapse point tracks the entropy of the answer's location, worsening in mid-context.' — TESTED in §14.1.
four_falsifiable_predictions.2_prompt: 'query-aware compression shifts the accuracy-versus-ratio curve to the right of query-agnostic compression by exactly the mutual-information gap.' — NOT tested by this paper; asserted from cited LongLLMLingua results [§5.1].
four_falsifiable_predictions.3_architectural: 'a state of s bits cannot answer a query requiring more than s bits, so state-space and linear-attention models exhibit a hard accuracy cliff on multi-key recall at a key count proportional to state size, while attention degrades gracefully.' — NOT tested by this paper; rests on cited theory [117] and [44] [§12].

seven_axis_taxonomy.source: [rate-distortion-compaction §3; layer-wise values in Table 2; per-method values in Appendix A Table 6]
axes: (1) Granularity of the compressed unit — bit-width, hidden dimension or rank, token / KV entry, page or block, layer or head, natural-language span, dense soft token, recurrent state, semantic item, visual token, inter-agent message.

(2) Lifecycle stage — architecture and pretraining; prompt/prefill time; prefill-to-decode KV formation; decode-time dynamic selection; the serving runtime across requests; within-task working-context curation; between-task consolidation; offline corpus indexing.
(3) Lossiness and fidelity — lossless reuse, near-lossless, uniformly lossy, or multi-fidelity; cross-cutting: reversible vs irreversible (P-rev).
(4) Query/task adaptivity — query-agnostic and offline-cacheable, query-conditioned and online, or task-aware via a learned reward (P-q); plus which importance signal is used.
(5) Learnability — training-free heuristic, post-training adapter, trained-from-scratch architecture, RL-learned policy, or LLM-as-controller with no weight change.

(6) Mechanism — drop/evict, select/retrieve (keep all), merge/cluster, quantize/encode, factorize/low-rank, abstractive summarize/rewrite, encode-to-latent, recurrent write–forget, structure/graph build, or internalize-to-weights.
(7) Storage substrate — on-GPU KV, a host/SSD/remote tier, model parameters, an external text or vector store, a knowledge graph, in-context dense vectors, or a hybrid parametric/nonparametric store.
seven_axis_taxonomy.which_axes_actually_separate_the_layers: 'The differences sit in three columns: granularity, lifecycle, and adaptivity. These are the three dimensions the lens flags as decisive, and the remaining axes vary far less across layers.' [§3, after the axis list]
seven_axis_taxonomy.note_for_v2: [해설] Axis (7) 'model parameters' and axis (6) 'internalize-to-weights' are exactly S0's Θ-path; axis (7) 'external text or vector store' is the E-path; axis (1) 'recurrent state' is the W-path. So the taxonomy CONTAINS the three-path split of S0 §2.3 as axis values, but the paper never treats the split as load-bearing — it explicitly demotes learnability and substrate as the axes that 'vary far less'.

update_layer.verdict: None exclusively. This paper does not instantiate (U-W), (U-Θ) or (U-E) — it states a CONSTRAINT that all three must satisfy simultaneously. It is the only paper in the v2 corpus whose contribution is layer-indifferent by construction.
update_layer.the_paper_s_own_statement: 'The bound holds for any compact memory Z, whether a KV cache, a gist vector, a recurrent state, or an agent's note store, which is what lets it unify the field.' [§2, ¶4] and 'there is no architecture-specific escape' [§2, consequence (i)].

mapping_onto_S0_s_three_rules.U-E: The paper's canonical instance. Its 𝓗 = 'the accumulated trace of an agent's life: tool calls, observations, dialogue turns, and prior reflections' and its Z = 'an external, mostly natural-language store of summaries, extracted facts, structured notes, or a knowledge graph', with U = 'a retrieval step that pages a subset of Z back into the window before generation' [§7, ¶1]. In S0 notation cmp_Θ(𝓗) IS S0's S(c_k; B_s) and wr(E_k, ·), and use(Z,q) IS ret(E,q) composed with f in (R). Its own Experiment 2 [§14.2] is a pure (U-E) experiment.
mapping_onto_S0_s_three_rules.U-W: Covered as §6 'Architectural and Bounded-State Compaction'. The paper's specialization is that S0's W has a fixed bit-size C_W set at training time: 'B = s is fixed once, before any query is seen' [§6, ¶1]. Its prediction (3) is a statement about (U-W): a hard accuracy cliff at a key count proportional to state size. It cites Titans [6] as 'a learned C_θ that re-optimizes its own distortion surrogate online' [§6] — i.e. the paper reads (U-W) as an online-learned compaction operator, which is a genuinely useful re-reading for the monograph.
mapping_onto_S0_s_three_rules.U-Θ: The thinnest coverage, and deliberately so: 'Weight-level compression (pruning, distillation, weight quantization) is out of scope' [§1, final ¶]. What survives is Θ as a STORAGE SUBSTRATE (axis 7 'model parameters', axis 6 'internalize-to-weights'), instantiated by Context Distillation [§5.2], Cartridges [§5.2], ROME/MEMIT [§7], and Nichani et al.'s parametric-capacity result [§12]. The paper's Θ-relevant claim is a capacity accounting one: 'facts already amortized into parameters contribute zero to I(Y;H|Q)' [§12], i.e. a successful (U-Θ) write REDUCES I★(q) and therefore relaxes the bound on the other two layers.
mapping_onto_S0_s_three_rules.the_fourth_thing: [평가] The paper's dominant object — the KV cache — has no letter in S0 §2.1. S0's three-way split (Θ / W / E) leaves the non-parametric attention state unnamed, and NM's Rosetta table (STYLE §3) calls it 'non-parametric memory state; softmax attention = capacity 무한의 associative memory'. §§4, 8, 11 of this paper (KV eviction, trainable sparse attention, serving substrate) all live there. The capacity chapter must either (a) name it explicitly as the C→∞ limit of W, following STYLE §1.6's 'softmax attention = 압축하지 않는 극한 (f→∞, capacity 무한)', or (b) admit a fourth store. Option (a) is consistent with the existing style document and is recommended.

update_layer.order_if_more_than_one: The paper argues explicitly that the layers are NOT sequential stages of one pipeline but three tiers of one hierarchy running at different timescales, all answering the same Eq. (1): KV cache 'sub-second, on-GPU, near-lossless at the granularity of a token'; working context 'inside the context window for the span of a task'; long-term store 'external and semantic, persists across sessions'. 'Their timescales span many orders of magnitude, but all three answer the same Eq. (1).' [§10.1; Figure 4]
update_layer.how_it_differs_from_the_canonical_forms: S0's (U-W)/(U-Θ)/(U-E) are all UPDATE rules: they say how the state moves. This paper supplies no update rule at all. It supplies (a) an objective the update rule should be minimizing (Eq. 1), (b) a floor no update rule can beat (Eq. 2), and (c) three binary properties (P-rev, P-q, P-fid) that predict which update rules fail. [해설] In the monograph this makes it a Part III paper wearing Part II clothes: it belongs to the 용량 axis of S0 §3.1, not to any single path.

cost_table.preamble: Reported strictly per S0 §2.4. Where the paper is silent the entry is exactly 'absent'. No estimation, no inference. Numbers reproduced at the paper's own precision.

B_s.detail: The paper never reports a sleep-time compute budget in FLOPs or tokens, for any method, anywhere. The nearest quantities are (a) the SWEEP VARIABLE of Experiment 2 — 'the number of compaction events', plotted over 5 to 25 events [Figure 6 x-axis, §14.2] — which is a count of LLM calls, not a budget; and (b) a qualitative statement that at the agent tier the compaction decision is itself an LLM call: 'every compaction event is an LLM call, so the savings a smaller context buys are partly repaid in inference overhead' [§7, ¶1] and 'agent consolidation is itself an expensive, error-prone LLM call, so the agent tier pays a budget the cache does not: the cost of deciding what to keep' [§10.4]. Neither is quantified. The paper's amortization argument for Letta STC — 'amortizing the per-compaction LLM-call cost across future queries' [§7] — carries no N_q and no cost figure.
B_s.finding: [평가] For a paper whose thesis is a budget/quality frontier, the total absence of any sleep-side compute number is itself the finding. Its budget axis is exclusively a STATE budget (bytes), never a COMPUTE budget. S0's amortization identity (A), C_avg = C_wake + C_sleep/N_q, cannot be instantiated from this paper at all.

L_w.detail: No measured latency number of any kind (ms/token, TTFT, TPOT) appears in the paper. What appears: (a) order-of-magnitude timescale labels in Figure 4 — 'KV cache: sub-token, on-GPU, microseconds, near-lossless, one forward pass' / 'Working context: tokens, in-window, milliseconds to seconds, within a task' / 'Long-term store: semantic items, external, hours to days, across sessions'; (b) the comparative statement 'KV compaction is a microsecond arithmetic decision, whereas agent consolidation is itself an expensive, error-prone LLM call' [§10.4]; (c) a REQUIREMENT rather than a measurement — COMPACT-Bench's third piece 'reports accuracy, latency, memory, and dollar cost together on one sheet, because a frontier that ignores decode latency or store cost conceals the very trade a deployment has to make' [§13.2]; (d) DistServe is described as 'optimizing TTFT and TPOT independently for goodput' [§11], a description of a cited system, not a measurement. Experiment 1 and Experiment 2 report accuracy and recall only — no latency column.

items: Haris & Onak [44]: 'any algorithm performing exact attention-based generation over a length-n, dimension-d context must use Θ(nd) space, with a matching Ω(d·e^d) barrier in the low-dimensional regime and no non-adaptive sublinear-time online attention.'

Wen et al. [117]: 'fixed-size RNN/SSM states provably cannot solve the in-context associative recall or tree recognition that attention solves, that chain-of-thought alone does not close the gap, and that a single attention layer (or RAG) restores it.'

Nichani et al. [83]: 'transformers store facts as associative memories whose capacity scales linearly in parameter count, with a single attention-plus-MLP block near-optimal.' — the paper's Θ-capacity anchor.
Xiao et al. [123]: 'retaining ∼4 sink tokens plus a sliding window streams to millions of tokens.'

Gu et al. [41]: sinks 'are universal, emerge only after enough optimization, act as key biases that absorb surplus attention without contributing to value computation, and vanish under un-normalized (sigmoid) attention.'

Ran-Milo [94]: 'for a natural family of trigger-conditional tasks, any softmax model that solves them must develop a sink' — hence 'evicting them is not lossy compression but a violation of budget feasibility in (1)'.
de Llano et al. [26]: sinks and depth-localized 'compression valleys' (sharp drops in residual-stream rank) are 'two faces of the same massive-activation mechanism concentrated in middle layers'.
Liu et al. [68]: 'a U-shaped recall curve: accuracy is highest when the evidence sits at the context's start or end and collapses in the middle.'
Tishby et al. [109] / Wang et al. [115]: the IB objective and its operationalization for context compression.
theory_results_collected_not_proved_here.the_gap_the_theory_leaves: 'Every result above is worst-case or mechanistic, and none predicts the 80–93% KV reductions and ∼20× prompt compression that practice routinely achieves... The gap between the lower bounds and observed compressibility is thus the gap between worst-case and data-conditional I★(Q), and that gap is not yet characterized.' [§12, final ¶]

the_prioritized_agenda.source: §15 'Open Problems and Research Agenda', 'ordered by impact times tractability'

items.title: Query-conditioned, reversible, multi-fidelity compaction at every layer
items.text: 'The single highest-leverage target follows directly from the bound... build operators that satisfy (P-q) and (P-rev) simultaneously, with a (P-fid) profile that keeps a cheap lossy tier over a small recoverable high-fidelity tier, and to do so at each tier of the hierarchy, porting the query-conditioned, no-evict design of Quest [108] and the retrieval-backing of InfiniGen [57] up into prompt and agent memory. This is tractable because the components exist in isolation; the work is composing them and showing the predicted right-shift (Prediction 2) and flat error curve (Prediction 4).'

items.title: Information-loss attribution and calibrated compaction confidence
items.text: 'Because the surrogate scorers of Section 2 are all estimators of one distortion, they can in principle emit a calibrated estimate of residual I★(Q), a per-decision compaction confidence with provenance of loss. A method that knows it has fallen below B < I★(Q) can defer, fetch, or escalate fidelity; this attribution is the prerequisite for everything adaptive below.'

items.title: A composition map for stacking operators
items.text: 'Quantization, low-rank projection, eviction, and merging are treated as independent recipes, yet stacking them compounds or cancels distortion, and serving-level lossless reuse (RadixAttention; 145) directly conflicts with lossy budgeting (InfiniGen; 57)... We stress that this is a measured map, not a set of proven laws: distortion surrogates are not additive and composition order matters.'

items.title: A predictive compression scaling law
items.text: 'The bound makes the compression ratio at fixed quality scale as 1/I★(Q), but I★(Q) is never measured directly. The open problem is a predictive law that estimates I★(Q), and hence the achievable ratio, as a function of model size, context length, head and layer structure, and task type, closing the gap between worst-case lower bounds (Θ(nd), sink necessity) and the reported 80–93% KV reductions. Such a law would turn budget selection from tuning into calculation.' — also named in §12 as 'the central unsolved problem this survey leaves open'.

items.title: An episodic-to-semantic consolidation bridge and a stop rule
items.text: 'Within-task curation (ACON; 53, Context-Folding; 105) and cross-session memory (Mem0; 21, MemGPT; 86) use disjoint mechanisms with no principled promotion from a lossless, recoverable episodic tier to a lossy, abstracted semantic tier. The formalism supplies the missing pieces: promote a span only when its marginal I★ over the query distribution justifies abstracting it, and, because repeated irreversible summarization grows error super-linearly (Prediction 4), adopt an output-error stop rule for agent summarization in the spirit of Ada-KV's bound.'
items.v2_relevance: This is the CLS/consolidation question of S0's 공통조상 block, restated as a promotion rule with a budget test.

items.title: Cheap, asynchronous, RL-stable agent self-curation
items.text: 'Reflection, note-, and update-based memory is LLM-call-heavy and self-reinforcing: it spends calls that erode the savings and stores errors that bias all future retrieval. The target is curation that is asynchronous (off the critical path, as sleep-time compute [65] begins to be), learned rather than hand-triggered (MemAct; 141, MEM1; 148), and stable under RL so the reward does not collapse into degenerate forgetting.'
items.v2_relevance: The paper's single most direct statement about sleep-time compute as a research direction. Note 'begins to be' — it treats Letta STC as an incomplete instance, not a solution.

items.title: Multimodal × multi-agent shared-memory compaction
items.text: 'Nobody has compacted multimodal context shared across collaborating agents, where the governing quantity is cross-modal versus inter-message redundancy under per-agent query distributions, a clean multi-source instance of objective (1).'

items.title: Adaptivity with guarantees
items.text: 'The bound says the right allocation equalizes the residual I★(Q) across units, budgeting by marginal task-utility rather than uniform ratio, so the open problem is content- and query-adaptive allocation that comes with a guarantee on the resulting distortion rather than an empirical sweep.'

items.title: Safety, auditability, and rollback of evolving memory
items.text: 'Self-editing memory that satisfies (P-rev) for utility also creates an attack surface: poisoning, leakage, and irreversible drift (AgentPoison; 18, MINJA; 30). Reversibility cuts both ways, enabling rollback and audit but also persistent injection, so the agenda is auditable, version-able compacted memory with a forgetting and revocation primitive.'

buried_in_body_sections.question: 'Composition is the open frontier. Quantization, low-rank, and eviction attack orthogonal axes, yet whether their errors compound or cancel, and which combinations help, remains largely uncharted, and it is where a rate–distortion account should be doing the design work.'

'Their intersection has no information-theoretic account... The bound of Eq. (2) is stated for a single Z answering a single Q, and it says nothing yet about how to size a shared B when agents draw different I★(Q) from one compressed multimodal store, or how irreversible visual merging collides with the provenance a downstream agent may later need. We still lack a theory that quantifies how much visual and temporal redundancy is compressible without task loss.'
buried_in_body_sections.note: An explicit admission that the bound does not extend to multi-consumer stores — directly relevant to any per-user shared memory in a serving fleet.

buried_in_body_sections.question: 'The last knob, a calibrated stop rule for when compaction has gone too far, exists at the KV layer as an output-error bound [34] and is all but absent for agent summarization, a gap the bridge brings into view.' Table 4 caption: 'an empty cell (a principled stop rule for agent summarization) is a research opportunity the alignment makes visible.'

Which cross-tier ports are clean and which need adaptation, given that (a) 'a KV cache that keeps a token's entries can attend to it exactly, while a store that keeps a summary of an episode has already paid an irreversible distortion', (b) at the KV tier the query 'is the next-token computation, implicit in the current hidden state; at the agent tier it is a future user request, genuinely unknown and possibly adversarial', and (c) 'the agent tier pays a budget the cache does not: the cost of deciding what to keep'.

'When should KV stay reversible and exact, paying storage and bandwidth, and when should it go lossy and cheap, paying distortion? And how does one stop a lossy decision made for a single request from silently degrading every descendant that later reuses it?'
buried_in_body_sections.note: The sharpest systems question in the paper.

buried_in_body_sections.question: Why Infini-attention 'proved hard to reproduce, which the formalism reads as a missing content-aware write policy: it spends s without a surrogate for what to overwrite.' — an unresolved reproduction failure, offered with an explanation but no test.
'estimating I★(Q) for real tasks is itself open' — the paper's own formalism rests on a quantity nobody can compute.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper's central quantity, I★(q), is never measured — not once, for any task, by this paper or any paper it cites. The bound (Eq. 2) therefore cannot be numerically evaluated anywhere in the survey; every use of it is qualitative ('below I★(Q) errors are forced'). The authors concede this twice.
unfavorable_facts.source: Limitations: 'The lower bound (Eq. 2) assumes a query-agnostic operator for its cleanest form and treats the task-conditioned information content I★(Q) as given; estimating I★(Q) for real tasks is itself open (Section 12).' Also §12, final ¶: 'I★(Q) is never measured directly.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: The survey's own claim to novelty over prior surveys is 'a single optimization objective with a provable bound rather than a descriptive grouping' [§1, ¶6]. If the bound's only free parameter is uncomputable, the bound organizes the field but never adjudicates any design decision numerically.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The bound's derivation assumes a query-agnostic operator. The Markov chain step 'Y − H − Z is Markov given Q' is asserted 'for a query-agnostic C'; the paper does not state or prove the corresponding bound for the query-conditioned operators that the entire §15 agenda advocates building.
unfavorable_facts.source: §2, ¶4: 'Because Ŷ = U(Z,Q) is a function of (Z,Q) and, for a query-agnostic C, the chain Y − H − Z is Markov given Q, the data-processing inequality gives...' — and Limitations: 'The lower bound (Eq. 2) assumes a query-agnostic operator for its cleanest form.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: Consequence (iii), the H(q) gap, is the paper's most-cited result and is a COMPARISON between query-agnostic and query-conditioned operators — but only one side of that comparison is derived.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The entire empirical contribution runs on one 1.5B model on one 8 GB consumer GPU, at 2k–8k context — three orders of magnitude below the long-context regime the survey is about (its own §1 motivates the problem with 'a hundred thousand tokens', §13.1 cites 115K-token and 11M-token results).
unfavorable_facts.source: §14, ¶1: 'a single commodity GPU, an NVIDIA RTX 4060 with 8 GB, using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct'; §14.1: 'contexts of 2k to 8k tokens'. Limitations: 'runs at reference scale... its absolute numbers should be read as illustrations of the methodology, not as a leaderboard.'

unfavorable_facts.fact: In Experiment 1 the six compaction methods are not distinguishable from a random-eviction control in any way the paper is willing to defend. The random control 'stays competitive' at high budget, and the authors themselves write off both the gaps and the ranking.
unfavorable_facts.source: §14.1, final ¶: 'The gaps are modest at this scale, and the ordering of methods is beside the point; what matters is the comparability the BPT axis delivers.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: The paper's thesis is that distortion surrogates differ in quality and are transferable across layers (§2, §10.3). Its own experiment supplies no evidence that ANY surrogate beats random at a fixed budget — it only shows the collapse below ~25% budget, which the random control also exhibits.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Prediction (4) claims SUPER-LINEAR error growth in the number of compaction events. The experiment does not establish super-linearity: it reports an interval (irreversible recall 'between 0.33 and 0.56' over 5–25 events, 'weakest at the highest compaction frequency') with no fitted curve, no exponent, and no comparison against a linear-growth null.
unfavorable_facts.source: Prediction stated in §2 (prediction 4), §7 final subsection, and §13.2 ('it should climb super-linearly'). Result reported in §14.2 and Figure 6 caption: 'irreversible memory loses roughly half its facts at every frequency' — note 'at every frequency', which reads as roughly FLAT-and-bad, not accelerating.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: The paper's Conclusion lists this as one of 'two results [that] stand out'. What was actually demonstrated is a level gap between reversible and irreversible operators, not the compounding dynamics the prediction asserts.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Experiment 2's two operators are not matched on compute or on state budget in any accounted way. The paper asserts they are 'at the same average budget' but reports no BPT value, no archive size, no retrieval index cost, and no count of summarizer LLM calls for either arm. BPT is defined only in the KV currency of Experiment 1.
unfavorable_facts.source: §14.2: 'Two operators at the same average budget therefore part by roughly 0.5 in recall'; the BPT definition at §14, ¶2 covers 'token eviction... b-bit quantization... prompt or summary compression to m of n tokens' but the reversible arm keeps ALL chunks in an archive, which the BPT formula does not price.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: The survey's headline methodological complaint is that the field compares methods on incommensurable budgets [§13.2]. Its own agent-layer experiment does exactly that: an operator that retains the full history is compared, at nominally 'the same average budget', against one that does not.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Only two of the four falsifiable predictions are tested. Prediction (2), the mutual-information right-shift, and prediction (3), the fixed-state accuracy cliff, are supported entirely by citing other people's results.
unfavorable_facts.source: §2, final sentence: 'We test (1) and (4) directly in Section 14.' Prediction (2) support = §5.1's reading of LongLLMLingua; prediction (3) support = §12's citation of Wen et al. [117] and Haris & Onak [44].

unfavorable_facts.fact: COMPACT-Bench is the authors' own benchmark, its evaluation criteria (multi-budget / cross-layer / repeated-compaction) are the authors' own, and Table 5 scores every existing benchmark against those criteria with COMPACT-Bench as the final row.
unfavorable_facts.source: §13.2 and Table 5. Also Table 1 does the same for surveys: it scores seven prior surveys against eight columns and marks the authors' own three claimed novelties ('RD/IB objective', 'X-layer transfer', 'Unified benchmark') — 'Recent surveys span the first four columns (notably 47); our novelty is the last three.' [Table 1 caption]
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: Both comparison tables are self-authored on self-chosen axes. In the vendored text the ●/◐/○ glyphs of Tables 1 and 5 are garbled, so the specific cell claims cannot even be audited from this copy.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper advertises 'the explicit transfer of mechanisms between layers' as one of four claimed novelties, but no ported mechanism is ever implemented or tested. All three ports in §10.3 are proposals.
unfavorable_facts.source: Novelty claim: §1, ¶6 and Table 1 column 'X-layer transfer'. The ports: §10.3 — MemoryBank's Ebbinghaus curve 'drops straight in as a scoring alternative' for KV eviction; Quest's no-evict discipline 'gives agent memory a template'; Ada-KV's output-error bound 'supplies the stop rule agent summarization lacks'. None is run. The only cross-tier evidence offered is EM-LLM [35], someone else's system.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: One of the three columns on which the survey claims superiority over prior surveys is, at the end of the paper, still entirely programmatic.

unfavorable_facts.fact: §3 promises that 'Appendix A carries the full per-method classification of roughly seventy methods'. Appendix A's Table 6 classifies 35 methods and is titled 'Master Method-by-Axis Table' with the caption 'Representative methods classified along the seven axes'.
unfavorable_facts.source: Promise: §3, final ¶. Delivery: Appendix A opening — 'Table 6 classifies representative methods from across the survey along the seven axes of Section 3'; the table's rows are 10 KV + 6 Prompt + 5 Arch + 6 Agent + 4 Sparse + 2 MM + 2 Sys = 35.
unfavorable_facts.caveat_on_this_finding: The row count is from the vendored plain-text extraction; a PDF-layout table could in principle lose rows in extraction. Recorded in todo_verify with a search term.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Table 3, the survey's headline KV comparison table, carries the same defect the survey exists to fix: its numbers are not comparable. The caption says so.
unfavorable_facts.source: Table 3 caption: 'Reductions are reported KV savings from the cited works and are not directly comparable across setups.' Compare §13.2: 'The units never line up, so the frontiers are incommensurable and each method's budget is set by whoever wrote the paper.'

unfavorable_facts.fact: The paper takes two incompatible positions on sleep-time compute and never reconciles them. §7 charges it with the query-agnostic penalty ('it spends budget speculatively on bits that may never be queried, the dual of the query-agnostic penalty H(Q) in Eq. (2)'); §10.5's principle P4 then recommends it ('sleep-time consolidation [65] move[s] the decision off the critical path and learn[s] it'); §15's sixth item hedges ('asynchronous (off the critical path, as sleep-time compute [65] begins to be)'). No quantity is offered that would say when the amortization beats the H(q) penalty.
unfavorable_facts.source: §7, 2nd family, final sentences; §10.5, P4; §15, sixth item.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts_v2_specifically: [평가] This is the exact tradeoff S0's amortization identity (A) is meant to arbitrate, and the paper that supplies the formal machinery declines to instantiate it. The monograph must supply N_q itself or admit the identity is unresolvable from the literature — which is already S0 §7's standing caveat ('실제 서빙에서 N_q 분포는 어느 논문도 보고하지 않음').

unfavorable_facts.fact: The 'roughly 80–93% KV reductions and ∼20× prompt compression that practice routinely achieves, with quantization reportedly within ∼2.7× of the information-theoretic limit' is stated in §12 with no per-number citation and no source for the 2.7× figure in that sentence.
unfavorable_facts.source: §12, final ¶. Compare §1's own scope statement: 'Much of the literature is recent and unrefereed, so we treat preprint numbers as provisional and flag results that have not been reproduced.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: These three numbers are the empirical anchor for the paper's headline theory gap (worst-case vs data-conditional I★(q)), and they are the least sourced numbers in the paper.

unfavorable_facts.fact: The architectural (W) layer, the layer whose bound is stated most sharply (prediction 3, 'a state of s bits cannot answer a query whose answer requires more than s bits'), receives no experiment at all. Neither does the prompt layer.
unfavorable_facts.source: §14 contains exactly two experiments, on the KV layer and the agent layer. §6 and §5 contribute no measurements.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_hurts: The survey's claim is that one budget axis unifies four layers; its demonstration of that axis covers two.

unfavorable_facts.fact: Experiment 2 leaves the experimental setup underspecified to a degree that blocks replication: the document length, chunk size, chunk count, retrieval method, and the identity of the summarizing model are all unstated. Only 'a long document', 'in chunks', 'twelve key–value facts' and 'an LLM-generated summary' are given.
unfavorable_facts.source: §14.2, full text of the setup paragraph. 'Code and configurations accompany the survey' [§14, ¶1] but no URL appears in the vendored text.

cross_path_citations.the_finding: [평가] This is the sharpest cross-path silence in the v2 corpus, and it runs in the direction the monograph should report. The paper cites Letta's Sleep-time Compute four times and builds a design principle (P4) and an agenda item (§15 sixth) around it — so it is genuinely inside the E-path conversation. Yet it cites ZERO of the six Θ-path sleep papers and ZERO of the two W-path sleep papers on S0's roster, and it explicitly rules weight-level work out of scope. The consequence is that the only paper in the corpus with a layer-agnostic capacity bound never applies that bound to the two paths that actually write to weights. Conversely, none of the Θ-path or W-path sleep papers can have cited this one (it is dated 2026-07-09, after all of them except Can-a-LM-Learn-Facts 2607.11020), so the silence is at present one-directional and unrebutted. The monograph's 분기 장 should state exactly this: the rate–distortion account of what to keep was written for E and for the KV cache, and its extension to Θ and W is available but unperformed.

systems_implications.framing_for_the_v2_reader: [해설] The reader's standing question is '그래서 그게 decode에서 뭘 바꾸는데?'. This paper's answer is unusual: it changes nothing in the decode kernel, and instead supplies the accounting unit in which every decode-side memory decision can be compared. What follows separates what the paper states (with location) from note-writer inference (marked [추론]).

decode_cost.claim: At long context and large batch the cache, not the weights, dominates both GPU memory and decode bandwidth, because 'every layer rereads every cached key and value at every step'.
'Run a transformer over a hundred thousand tokens and the cached keys and values of everything it has already read take up more of the accelerator than the model's own weights.'

Sparse-retrieval methods (Quest, Landmark Attention) change decode BANDWIDTH, not capacity. 'These methods cut bandwidth, not capacity: they convert what to forget into what to fetch, which is why the bound's I★(Q) penalty does not bind on them as it does on evictors.' Table 3 marks Quest's reduction as 'read-only'.
decode_cost.why_it_matters: For a decode-bound serving system this is the distinction that decides whether a method buys HBM capacity or HBM traffic. The paper is unusually explicit about it.

decode_cost.claim: The same caveat applies to the retrieval-augmented architectural family: 'these methods sparsify retrieval but not storage. The full KV still lives somewhere, so the true rate(Z) is unchanged and the compression is of compute, not memory.'

Prefill and decode have different compaction needs and should get different budgets: 'SCOPE [119] observes that prefill and decode have different compaction needs, since decoding accumulates its own heavy hitters, and allocates separate KV budgets to the two phases with a sliding decode strategy, dropping the assumption built into decode-time evictors that one budget fits both stages of the lifecycle.'

state_bytes_moved.claim: The layer-agnostic accounting unit is BPT = retained bytes / raw history tokens, with three explicit conversions: eviction keeping fraction f costs f; b-bit quantization costs b/16; prompt or summary compression to m of n tokens costs m/n; full cache = 1.0.
state_bytes_moved.worked_reading: [추론] At the paper's fp16 reference, 2-bit quantization sits at b/16 = 0.125 BPT and 4-bit at 0.25 BPT; an evictor at 25% of the cache also sits at 0.25 BPT. The paper's Experiment 1 says every method is 'at or near zero accuracy' below roughly 0.25 BPT [§14.1], so on ITS task and ITS model a 4-bit quantizer and a 4× evictor sit at the same point on the axis where eviction has already failed. The paper does not draw this comparison itself — it is note-writer inference from the BPT formula plus the §14.1 collapse threshold, and it is exactly the kind of comparison the BPT axis was built to make.

state_bytes_moved.claim: Per-token KV byte formula (layers × kv-heads × head-dim × 2 tensors × dtype bytes)

state_bytes_moved.claim: In disaggregated serving, rate(Z) reappears as a BANDWIDTH budget rather than an occupancy budget: 'Splitwise [89], DistServe [147], and Mooncake [92] disaggregate the two phases onto separate machines, which turns the KV cache into a tensor that must be transferred between prefill and decode pools over the interconnect... Here rate(Z) returns not as an occupancy budget but as a bandwidth budget: the cost of an exact, reversible representation is the time to ship it, which is what makes the lossy and the transmissible families below attractive even when memory is not scarce.'
state_bytes_moved.why_it_matters: [해설] This is the paper's most directly useful systems sentence for the monograph: it shows that the SAME budget C can be denominated in HBM bytes, in interconnect bytes, or in tokens, and that the choice of denomination is what makes a method look good or bad.

batching.what_the_paper_says: One sentence only: 'At long context and large batch it is the cache, not the weights, that dominates GPU memory and decode bandwidth.' [§4, ¶1]
batching.what_it_does_not_say: The paper performs no batching analysis. It does not discuss how per-request compaction state interacts with shared-weight batching, does not discuss grouped-GEMM decode, and does not discuss whether per-request BPT budgets can be scheduled jointly across a batch. Its Experiment 1 and 2 are single-stream.
batching.finding: [평가] For a paper whose §11 is titled 'Systems and Serving Substrate', the absence of any batching treatment is a real gap. NM's pair thesis — that per-request fast-weight state breaks shared-weight batching (STYLE §3, Rosetta row 'batching') — has no counterpart here, even though the paper's own §11 tension (lossless reuse vs lossy budgeting) is fundamentally a multi-request scheduling problem.

memory_hierarchy_landing.what_lands: the KV cache; 'sub-token, on-GPU, microseconds, near-lossless, one forward pass'

CachedAttention 'stretches the horizon across conversational turns, spilling KV to DRAM and SSD tiers with layer-wise prefetch to hide slow-tier latency'; FlexGen 'aggregates GPU, CPU, and disk, solves a linear program for tensor placement, and quantizes weights and the cache to four bits'; InfiniGen 'keeps only a working set on-GPU, rehearsing the next layer with partial weights to guess which few tokens will matter and prefetching only their KV from host memory'; ShadowKV 'offloads the value cache, retains a low-rank key cache plus landmarks and outliers, and reconstructs keys to fetch only the values it needs'; Mooncake 'pools idle CPU, DRAM, and SSD across the cluster into a disaggregated KVCache store driven by a cache-centric scheduler'.

CacheGen 'encodes the cache into a compact bitstream that exploits its layer- and token-locality and streams it, trading a controlled, near-lossless quantization error for far lower transfer time'; CacheBlend 'reuses each chunk's independently precomputed KV and recomputes only the small fraction of cross-attention entries that the chunks' new neighbors change' — 'a multi-fidelity operator (P-fid) in the wild: a large reused tier plus a tiny recomputed tier sized by an error budget'.

the_serving_hazard_worth_carrying_into_p.claim: Distortion is INHERITED through the prefix-reuse tree. 'Lossless reuse (PagedAttention, RadixAttention, prefix caches) assumes the stored KV is exactly what attention would have produced; lossy budgeting (InfiniGen, ShadowKV, quantized offload) assumes it may be approximated. Composing the two operators costs something: reusing a prefix that was itself evicted or quantized propagates the earlier distortion into every request that shares it, and the errors compound across the reuse tree instead of staying local to one sequence.'
the_serving_hazard_worth_carrying_into_p.open_question_it_states: 'When should KV stay reversible and exact, paying storage and bandwidth, and when should it go lossy and cheap, paying distortion? And how does one stop a lossy decision made for a single request from silently degrading every descendant that later reuses it?'
the_serving_hazard_worth_carrying_into_p.note: [해설] This is the systems statement that generalizes most directly to the sleep-time setting: a sleep-time artifact (a Cartridge, a consolidated E record, a Θ delta) is shared by every downstream request in exactly the way a cached prefix is, so any distortion written during sleep is inherited by all N_q wake queries — the amortization denominator of S0's identity (A) amortizes the ERROR as well as the cost. The paper does not say this about sleep-time compute; it says it about prefix caches. Marked as note-writer extension.

prefix_reuse_has_no_floor.claim: 'Their leverage comes not from spending fewer bits but from amortizing bits already spent, which is why the gains are entirely workload-dependent and collapse to nothing without prefix overlap. Reuse, unlike compression, buys nothing when there is nothing to reuse.'
prefix_reuse_has_no_floor.relevance: The exact structural analogue of S0's caveat that the amortization identity (A) presumes a known N_q. Reuse and sleep-time amortization share the same failure mode: no shared context, no gain.

the_cost_of_deciding_what_to_keep.claim: 'KV compaction is a microsecond arithmetic decision, whereas agent consolidation is itself an expensive, error-prone LLM call, so the agent tier pays a budget the cache does not: the cost of deciding what to keep.'
the_cost_of_deciding_what_to_keep.and_the_prescription: Principle P4: 'Make compaction asynchronous and learnable, not a blocking heuristic. When deciding what to keep is itself an LLM call on the critical path, it erodes the savings it buys. RL-learned policies [105, 141] and sleep-time consolidation [65] move the decision off the critical path and learn it; fixed-threshold auto-compaction does neither.' [§10.5]
the_cost_of_deciding_what_to_keep.relevance: [해설] This is the paper's own derivation of WHY sleep-time compute exists, arrived at from a rate–distortion premise rather than from a biological metaphor: the decision cost of compaction is itself a wake-time latency contribution L_w, and moving it off the critical path is the only way to stop it eating the savings. The monograph can use this as an independent, non-neuroscientific justification for the sleep/wake split.

the_five_design_principles_verbatim.P1: 'Never discard irreversibly what you cannot re-derive cheaply. At equal budget a reversible operator (retrieval-backed eviction, archival memory) weakly dominates an irreversible one (permanent eviction, lossy summarization): the two can differ only on queries whose evidence was dropped, and there the reversible one wins. Quest [108] follows P1; H2O [142] and fixed-schedule summarization violate it.'
the_five_design_principles_verbatim.P2: 'Condition on the query distribution, not just the current query. The bound charges a query-agnostic operator the entropy H(Q). Trainable sparse attention (Section 8) and query-aware compression [50] pay less of this penalty; offline gisting pays it in full.'
the_five_design_principles_verbatim.P3: 'Separate a cheap reversible episodic tier from a lossy semantic tier, with explicit promotion and demotion. Multi-fidelity memory (P-fid) dominates a single lossy tier: keep raw episodes cheaply and recoverably, and abstract only what proves reusable. MIRIX's typed modules [113] and the Compressive Transformer's dual tier [93] are built this way; a flat summarization buffer is not.'
the_five_design_principles_verbatim.P4: 'Make compaction asynchronous and learnable, not a blocking heuristic.' (full text above)
the_five_design_principles_verbatim.P5: 'Budget by marginal task-utility, not a uniform ratio. The bound is governed by I★(Q), which spreads unevenly across heads, layers, and memory items. Non-uniform allocation [11, 34] respects this; a global fixed ratio ignores it and spends budget on low-utility state.'

systems_implications.what_the_reader_should_take_to_the_capac: [평가] Three things, in order of durability. (1) The unit: BPT makes a KV evictor, a quantizer, a prompt compressor and an agent summary commensurable, and S0 §2.4's C should be denominated this way. (2) The floor: below I★(q) every layer errs at the same rate, so the three-path comparison of S0 §2.3 cannot be settled by architecture — only by how well each path estimates the distortion surrogate and whether it keeps (P-rev). (3) The penalty: sleep-time compute is query-agnostic by S0's own definition, so by consequence (iii) it pays H(q) — and the only escape the paper offers is (P-rev), i.e. a sleep-time path that keeps a recoverable tier rather than overwriting. That is a design constraint the monograph can state as a proposition, and it cuts against the Θ-path (weight edits are 'maximally irreversible', §7) and for the E-path (archives and temporal graphs retire rather than delete, §7).
